question: It is 1 October 2025. The photos in a rental ad look like they show mould in one of the bedrooms. Are they allowed to advertise it like that, and is the photo enough to prove the place doesn't meet the minimum standards?
answer:
**Short answer:** On 1 October 2025, the Act had no rule that specifically banned advertising a rental that didn't meet the minimum standards. That rule started on 25 November 2025. And a photo on its own doesn't prove the place fails the mould standard.

**Versions in force on 1 October 2025**
- *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, **Authorised Version 110** (rta-1997-v110-2025-08-06.pdf, in force 6 August 2025 to 24 November 2025) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf)
- *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, **Authorised Version 004** (rt-regs-2021-v004-2025-07-01.pdf, in force 1 July 2025 to 24 November 2025) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/21-3sra004-authorised.pdf)

---

### 1. Could they advertise it like that?

- **No advertising ban yet.** In Version 110, s 65A is followed directly by s 66 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf). There is no s 65B.
- **The ban came later.** Section 65B first appears in **Version 111** (rta-1997-v111-2025-11-25.pdf, in force from 25 November 2025). It says a rental provider or agent "must not advertise or otherwise offer premises to let unless… [they] reasonably believe the premises comply with the rental minimum standards." The penalty is 60 penalty units for a natural person and 300 for a body corporate [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). It doesn't apply on 1 October 2025.
- **What did apply:** under s 65A(1), the rental provider had to make sure the place met the minimum standards "on or before the day on which the renter enters into occupation." The penalty was 60 penalty units for a natural person and 300 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf). Version 004 of the Regulations set the infringement penalty for this offence at 12 penalty units for a natural person and 60 for a body corporate [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/21-3sra004-authorised.pdf). A penalty unit was worth $203.51 for 2025–26 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/21-3sra004-authorised.pdf).

### 2. Is the photo enough to prove a breach?

**The documents don't say a photo is enough.** The mould standard (Schedule 4, clause 8) says: "Each room in the rented premises must be free from mould and damp **caused by or related to the building structure**" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/21-3sra004-authorised.pdf). So the standard is only breached if the mould is linked to the building structure. A photo can show mould, but not what caused it. The documents don't say what evidence would be needed.

---

### What a prospective renter can do or ask

- **Ask about mould repair notices.** The rules on what a provider must tell applicants (reg 16(2)) include whether the place meets the minimum standards. They also include whether, in the last 3 years, the provider received a repair notice about mould or damp caused by or related to the building structure. This text appears in Version 002 [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf) and Version 005 [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). However, the part of Version 004 I retrieved doesn't include reg 16, so I can't confirm its exact wording on 1 October 2025.
- **Before moving in:** you can end the agreement by giving notice if the place "do[es] not meet any rental minimum standards" (s 91L(f)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).
- **On or right after moving in:** if the place doesn't meet the standards, you can ask the provider for urgent repairs (s 65A(2)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).
- **During the tenancy:** the provider must keep the place in good repair and reasonably fit to live in, even if you knew about the problem before moving in (s 68(1), (1A)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).

(1) It quotes the mould standard: 'Each room in the rented premises must be free from mould and damp caused by or related to the building structure.' (2) It says the photo alone doesn't prove a breach: 'a photo on its own doesn't prove the place fails the mould standard' and 'A photo can show mould, but not what caused it.' (3) It gives next steps, including asking about mould repair notices, ending the agreement before moving in under s 91L(f), and requesting urgent repairs under s 65A(2).

question: It is 15 October 2026. I let a friend move into my rental without telling the agent. Now I want them out. What do I have to do?
answer:
# Getting a friend you let move in to leave (Victoria, as at 15 October 2026)

**Short answer:** The documents don't explain how a renter removes a friend or sub-tenant. What they do show is that the arrangement may put your own tenancy at risk, so get advice before you act.

**Law that applies:** The *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, file **rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf (Authorised Version No. 115, in force from 13 October 2026)**. This was the version in force on 15 October 2026 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

---

## What the law says

**1. You needed written consent.** A renter must not assign or sub-let all or part of the property without the rental provider's **written consent** [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). A sub-letting without consent is **invalid** unless the Tribunal has decided consent wasn't needed [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**2. The rental provider could ask you to leave.** If you sub-let without consent, the rental provider can give you a notice to vacate. The move-out date must be **at least 14 days** after the notice is given [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Separately, you can also be given a notice to vacate (with at least 14 days) if any other person living there seriously threatens or intimidates the rental provider or agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**3. The rental provider can't remove you outside the Act.** Except as the Act allows, the rental provider or agent must not force or try to force you to leave. The penalty is up to **150 penalty units** for an individual or **750 for a company** [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**4. Your friend may have rights of their own:**
- If your friend has a sub-letting agreement with you and your own agreement ends, they can become the rental provider's renter, on the same terms as their agreement with you [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- If the property is their main home, they can ask the Tribunal to order the rental provider to give them their own agreement. They can do this once, for example, you give notice that you're leaving or a possession order is applied for [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal would have to be satisfied that they would suffer **severe hardship** if they had to leave, and that this would outweigh the rental provider's hardship [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

---

## What you can do or ask

**How to remove your friend:** The documents don't cover this. None of the retrieved material sets out how a renter can end a sub-tenant's or guest's stay. The notice to vacate form in the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (**rt-regs-2021-v009-2026-06-30.pdf, version 009, in force from 30 June 2026**) is for a rental provider giving notice to a renter. It isn't for a renter giving notice to their friend [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

**What to check first:**
- **Does your friend pay you rent or have an agreement with you?** This decides whether it counts as a sub-letting, which brings in the rules above [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf), [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Is the property their main home?** This affects whether they could ask the Tribunal for their own agreement [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Don't give notice to end your own tenancy to get them out.** Doing that can let your friend apply to the Tribunal for their own agreement [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
